trickyParts: The order of sessionEntryHandler's error arms is load-bearing and is pinned by a test, as recorded above. Reading it as a switch or reordering for readability turns a caller's bad key into a 503 the client retries.

The text `no live session <id>` is not wording: internal/dispatch/api/comment_delivery.go tests that exact prefix to decide whether a mention keeps its session pin, and the dashboard prints the string verbatim. Only ErrNotFound produces it; every other failure carries the listener's own reason through deliveryErrorText.

A broadcast refuses the whole send when one per-session read does not answer, and writes nothing, because a broadcast commits under its idempotency key and replayedExclusions answers "excluded by the original send" for every session the original missed. A transient failure turned into a stored exclusion would be frozen into that key for every retry the sender can make.

The mention's delivery still passes through the listener's send route, which reads the cache alone until dispatch://INFRA-141 lands. It succeeds because SessionRegistry.Refresh writes what it read into the cache, so the send that follows finds it — on the listener that answered the read. A deployment running more than one listener behind ENVOY_URL would still refuse the send until INFRA-141 merges. The cross-service proof asserts the delivery, so the reliance is visible rather than assumed.

roleHolderSession was deliberately not renamed and no helper was added for the 503 body, per the plan's D4 and D3: dispatch://INFRA-141 generalises that same function to liveSessionEntry and introduces the constant, and two branches growing two helpers of one name would meet as a conflict whose resolution deletes one. rigReconstruction.dockerStandIn:
Saved at "$TOOLS/shim/docker", first on PATH for the e2e-local.sh run only. It is not in the repository and is not a general docker: it implements `run`, `container inspect`, `stop` and `rm` for exactly the argv that script uses, starting the local nats-server in place of mirror.gcr.io/library/nats:2.10-alpine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

state_dir="${DOCKER_SHIM_DIR:-/legion/scratch/tmp/tools/docker-shim}"
mkdir -p "$state_dir"
nats_bin="${DOCKER_SHIM_NATS_BIN:-/legion/scratch/tmp/tools/bin/nats-server}"

pidfile_of() { printf '%s/%s.pid' "$state_dir" "$1"; }

alive() {
  local file pid
  file="$(pidfile_of "$1")"
  [[ -f "$file" ]] || return 1
  pid="$(cat "$file")"
  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null
}

case "${1:-}" in
  run)
    shift
    name=""
    port=""
    image=""
    server_args=()
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
      case "$1" in
        --name) name="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -d) shift ;;
        -p) port="${2%%:*}"; shift 2 ;;
        *)
          if [[ -z "$image" ]]; then image="$1"; else server_args+=("$1"); fi
          shift ;;
      esac
    done
    [[ -n "$name" && -n "$port" && -n "$image" ]] || { echo "docker-shim: unsupported run argv" >&2; exit 2; }
    alive "$name" && { echo "docker-shim: $name already running" >&2; exit 1; }
    data="$state_dir/$name.data"
    rm -rf "$data"
    mkdir -p "$data"
    "$nats_bin" --addr 127.0.0.1 --port "$port" --store_dir "$data" "${server_args[@]}" \
      >"$state_dir/$name.log" 2>&1 &
    echo $! >"$(pidfile_of "$name")"
    for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
      if (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port") 2>/dev/null; then exec 3<&-; break; fi
      sleep 0.1
    done
    cat "$(pidfile_of "$name")"
    ;;
  container)
    [[ "${2:-}" == "inspect" ]] || { echo "docker-shim: unsupported container subcommand" >&2; exit 2; }
    alive "${3:-}" || exit 1
    echo "[{\"Name\":\"/${3}\"}]"
    ;;
  stop)
    name="${2:-}"
    if alive "$name"; then kill "$(cat "$(pidfile_of "$name")")" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    sleep 0.3
    echo "$name"
    ;;
  rm)
    name="${2:-}"
    if alive "$name"; then kill -9 "$(cat "$(pidfile_of "$name")")" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    rm -rf "$(pidfile_of "$name")" "$state_dir/$name.data"
    echo "$name"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "docker-shim: unsupported command: ${1:-}" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
